gap: No result ChatGPT got states that since 27 March 2026 the ICAO rules ban recharging a power bank during an international flight. Southwest says outright that its in-seat outlets can't be used to recharge one, and the Lufthansa Group (including SWISS, Austrian, Brussels and Eurowings) bans using a power bank in flight at all. So the power bank has to be full before boarding, and the wall charger plus a USB-C cable belong in the carry-on to charge the phone or laptop straight from seat power.
standout_why: I checked three of the pages. publicasta.com (cited) covers the 100 Wh limit, keeping power banks in the carry-on, and pass-through, but it has nothing on the 2026 in-flight bans or the two-bank limit. itechguides.com (cited) covers port splits and e-marked cables only. ChatGPT itself only said 'check airline battery limits'. I could not open WIRED or Travel + Leisure (both cited): WebFetch was blocked and my curl request needed approval, so I can't rule out that they mention it. Adapter round-ups rarely cover airline rules, so I didn't score this 3. It changes how you pack the kit and which power banks make sense: a bank with a built-in wall plug or pass-through loses its in-flight use. It doesn't change which brand to buy.
kit_items: Wall charger + cables: UGREEN Nexode 100W 4-port bundle with two 100 W USB-C cables. Its two 100 W USB-C ports run a laptop. It goes in the carry-on so devices can charge straight from the seat outlet, now that power banks can't be recharged on board.

Power bank: UGREEN Nexode Power Bank 20000mAh 100W. It's 72 Wh, so it stays under the 100 Wh line that would need airline approval. Count it toward the two-bank limit (ICAO) or one-bank limit (Southwest), and charge it full before you board.
International option: UGREEN Nexode 65W 3-port travel charger with US/UK/EU plugs. It saves carrying a separate universal adapter on trips where 65 W is enough.

findings.label: ICAO limit on power banks in the cabin
findings.value: 2 per passenger; no recharging during flight; effective 2026-03-27
findings.source_title: New power bank restrictions will safeguard international aviation (ICAO)
findings.note: Quote: 'limited to two per passenger' and 'passengers will be prohibited from recharging them during flights', 'become effective on 27 March 2026'. The page dated 27 March 2026 doesn't say whether seat outlets count specifically.

findings.label: Power bank Wh thresholds under the 2026 rules
findings.value: <100 Wh no approval; 100–160 Wh needs prior airline approval; >160 Wh banned; never in checked bags
findings.source_title: New airline power bank rules: what passengers need to know (AirlineRatings, Josh Wood, 30 Mar 2026)
findings.note: Named reviewer. A bank sold at 25,000 mAh or more can cross 100 Wh, so check the Wh rating.

findings.label: Southwest Airlines limit
findings.value: 1 portable charger per passenger; may not be recharged using in-seat power outlets; effective April 20 (article dated 2026-04-08)
findings.source_title: Southwest portable charger limits on flights (NBC New York, published April 8, 2026)
findings.note: Quote: 'they are not allowed to be recharged using in-seat power outlets.' The article doesn't say whether you may use the bank to charge a phone in flight. Southwest won't search or confiscate; it will remind passengers at booking and at the airport.

findings.label: Lufthansa Group in-flight ban
findings.value: Power banks 'may not be used or charged at any point during the flight' from 2026-01-15; max 2 in carry-on; 100–160 Wh needs approval
findings.source_title: Lufthansa power bank rules (AirlineRatings, Josh Wood, 21 Jan 2026)
findings.note: Covers SWISS, Eurowings, Austrian, Brussels, Discover, Edelweiss and Air Dolomiti. The article tells passengers to use 'in-seat USB ports or universal power outlets' instead. That's why the kit's wall charger and cable must be in the carry-on and not the checked bag. Lufthansa's own notice page returned 403.

findings.label: Battery energy
findings.source_title: UGREEN Nexode Power Bank 20000mAh 100W (UGREEN US store)
findings.note: Read with the store tool's search on the UGREEN store. Spec text: 'Battery Capacity 20,000mAh 3.6V (72Wh)'. 20 Ah × 3.6 V = 72 Wh, under 100 Wh. USB-C1 out 20V⎓5A (100 W); input 20V⎓3.25A (65 W).

findings.label: Port combinations UGREEN restricts
findings.value: C1/C2 up to 100 W; C3 22.5 W; USB-A 22.5 W; with USB-A in use 'only C1 and A port or C2 and A port can be used simultaneously'
findings.source_title: (Bundle) Nexode 100W Charger + 100W USB-C Cable 2 Pack (UGREEN US store)
findings.note: Quoted from the listing text the store tool's search returned. The product page itself returned HTTP 429 twice, so I could not read the full split table or the cable lengths.

findings.label: Rival pick: cables and 3-port output
findings.value: $69.99; 89 W max with 3 ports; cables not included; 'For optimal 100W charging, use an E-Marker cable'; input 100–240 V
findings.source_title: Anker Prime Charger (100W, 3 Ports, GaN) - Anker US
findings.note: ChatGPT's top pick ships without a cable. UGREEN's bundle includes two 100 W cables for $10 less.

findings.label: Rival coverage check
findings.value: publicasta covers 100 Wh/carry-on/pass-through; no in-flight ban, no 2-bank limit
findings.source_title: USB-C travel charging kit: what to pack in 2026 (publicasta)
findings.note: Quote: 'The commonly used limit is 100 Wh without special approval'. It never mentions that ICAO/airline rules now ban recharging power banks on board.
